name: Alienware m16 R2 zones
notes: Unverified: never tried on this machine. Written on 2026-10-16 by alienfx.mjs from alienfx-tools, https://github.com/T-Troll/alienfx-tools, MIT licence, commit 3289c320 (2026-10-14): alienfx-gui/Mappings/devices.csv, each machine's map of its lights.
Its map there: “Alienware m16R2 (US)”, line 1239, device “m16 Tron lights”. Which id lights what is that map's; the names are its own, in plain words.
The protocol is verified: the AW-ELC's live preview, as alienware-m18-r1-zones.json sends it, which stores nothing in the device.

Matched on the machine (#326): SMBIOS names it “Alienware m16 R2”, as dmidecode reports it in linuxhw/DMI, https://github.com/linuxhw/DMI (CC BY 4.0), commit 57b21bc6 (2025-01-06): Notebook/Alienware/m16/m16 R2, SKU 0C91.
Left out: id 4, “Power”, which alienfx-tools marks as the power button: the firmware drives it, as on the m18 R1.
The m18 R1's built-in zones name no machine and describe 187c:0551 too: download this file and choose it on the device's card.
alienfx-tools names id 0 “haptic” and id 2 “back”, no more: drawn where its grid puts them, below the keyboard and on the lid.

Drawn from the front, lid open, the lights at the back seen through the hinge. Where a light sits is not in the source: the keyboard zones keep the order and widths of alienfx-tools' grid, the rest is drawn where its name puts it.
